chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
The first righteous deed a man does for his child is that he names it with a good name, so let each one of you give a good name to his child.

key_terms.يَبَرُّ: to do righteous deeds / to be kind to

ai.seo_question: What is the first righteous deed a father should do for his child according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni places this narration within the chapter on names, underscoring the Shia scholarly view that naming is a foundational act of parental duty (birr) that influences the child's identity and spiritual trajectory. The hadith highlights that selecting a virtuous name is the primary manifestation of kindness, reflecting the belief that a name carries inherent significance in Islamic tradition. This teaching aligns with the broader ethical framework where the parent's initial responsibility is to establish a positive spiritual and social foundation for the offspring.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Musa Bin Bakr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The first righteous deed the man does for his child is that he names it by a good name, so let each one of you give a good name to his child’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Ali from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “
The first good thing that a father can do to his children is to give them good names. You must find a good name for (each of) your children.’”
